cards.text: Right before this, enemy horses are heard snorting from Dan, and the whole land quakes. Now the prophet speaks, and friend, he is hurting. He says, 'My sorrow is beyond healing; my heart is faint within me.'

cards.question: The prophet says to listen to a cry from the daughter of his people, coming from a land far away. What are they asking?

answers.text: Whether the LORD is still in Zion
Whether Egypt will send them help
Whether the rain will ever return

cards.text: And right in the middle of their cry, the LORD speaks up with a question of His own.

cards.question: The LORD asks why His people have provoked Him to anger, and His question points straight at their ___.
The people's cry goes on: the harvest has passed and the summer has ended. True or false: they say they have finally been saved.

cards.text: Harvest gone, summer gone, still not saved, like waiting all day for the repair guy and the window closes and NOBODY ever knocks. And the prophet says, 'For the brokenness of the daughter of my people I am crushed.'

cards.question: Then the prophet asks, 'Is there no balm in Gilead? Is no physician there?' What is he really asking?

answers.text: Why his people still aren't healed
Where to find medicine for himself
When Gilead will send its army

cards.text: Then the prophet wishes his head were a spring of water and his eyes a fountain of tears. He says he would weep day and night over the slain daughter of his people.

cards.question: Right after all those tears, the prophet makes a wish about the wilderness. What does he wish he had out there?

answers.text: A traveler's lodge to leave his people
A quiet place to pray for his people
A well to bring his people water

cards.question: Why does the prophet say he would leave his own people behind?

cards.text: One verse he's weeping day and night, the next verse he wants a lodge in the wilderness with NO forwarding address. Friend, you can love people with your whole heart and still want to pack a bag.
Now the LORD speaks. He says, 'They bend their tongues like bows; lies prevail over truth in the land.'

cards.question: With lies everywhere in the land, what does the LORD tell everyone to do about his neighbor?
True or false: the LORD says a brother can still be trusted, even if a neighbor can't.

cards.text: They've taught their tongues to lie, and they wear themselves out committing iniquity. Friend, that's working OVERTIME at the wrong job.

cards.question: The LORD says His people dwell in the midst of deception. In their deceit, what does He say they refuse to do?

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says what He will do. He asks what else He can do, because of the daughter of His people.

cards.question: So what does the LORD of Hosts say He will do to His people?

answers.text: Give them a brand new king

cards.text: The LORD says their tongues are deadly arrows. They speak deception.

cards.question: The LORD describes a two-faced man: with his ___ he speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his ___ he sets a trap for him.

cards.text: That's the coworker who says 'LOVE that idea' in the meeting, then emails your boss about it before you're back at your desk.

cards.question: True or false: after all this, the LORD says He will simply overlook what this nation has done.

cards.text: Then a weeping and wailing goes up for the mountains, a dirge over the wilderness pasture.

cards.question: Why is there wailing over the mountains and the wilderness pasture?

answers.text: They've been scorched and left empty
A great flood has covered them
Strangers have fenced them all off

cards.question: True or false: out on that scorched land, even the birds of the air and the beasts have fled.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, 'And I will make Jerusalem a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.'

findings.problem: The speaker is introduced only as 'the prophet' and is never named anywhere in the walkthrough. When he first appears, the baker is never told it is Jeremiah.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card only recaps Jeremiah 9:1-2, which cards 8-10 already covered, and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so the joke has no new moment to ride on. It also states as fact that the prophet loves his people 'with your whole heart', without marking it as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 9:6 reads 'You dwell in the midst of deception; in their deceit they refuse to know Me.' The text does not say who 'You' is, and it sets 'You' apart from 'they'. The question settles it as 'His people dwell in the midst of deception', which closes a point the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about Jeremiah 9:8, which cards 8 and 9 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke also lands unclearly, because 'emails your boss about it' doesn't clearly show the trap behind the friendly words.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
